fact: Reporting on Namibia's 2025 AI Readiness Assessment lists no formal AI regulatory framework among its unresolved problems, as published by iAfrica on 2 October 2026 (assessment dated 2025, no month given).

At the 14 August 2025 launch of Namibia's first AI Readiness Assessment Report, NCRST's Dr Simeon Hamukoshi cited the absence of a formal AI regulatory framework as a persisting challenge, and the report recommends establishing a national AI governance framework.

ITWeb Africa reports the ICT minister saying government has prioritised a national AI strategy before introducing legislation, so no AI legislation has yet been introduced; the document's own date, 2026-08-05, is used.

Tech Africa News reports the ICT minister saying at a 3 August 2026 meeting that government has prioritised a national AI strategy before introducing legislation, so no AI legislation has yet been introduced.
Commentator Hafeni Kashimbonde writes of Namibia 'in the absence of explicit, standalone national AI laws', where parastatals remain bound by corporate governance and privacy law.
